title: BradEngine Software 3D Renderer

contributors.contribution: Jamie used the BradEngine 3D system while teaching his sons graphics, game programming, physics, and related technical concepts.

description: BradEngine included a native software 3D renderer written in JavaScript and rendered through HTML5 Canvas. I built the core 3D pipeline myself, including mesh loading, world and camera transforms, perspective projection, culling, polygon depth sorting, lighting, procedural geometry, mesh morphing, rigid-body and soft-body physics synchronization, terrain, and height-map-driven rendering.

sections.title: Custom Software 3D Pipeline
paragraphs: The renderer was a native BradEngine subsystem rather than a wrapper around an external rendering engine.
BradEngine transformed and projected 3D mesh data itself before drawing polygons to HTML5 Canvas.

sections.title: Transform & Camera Pipeline
paragraphs: The renderer implemented reusable model, world, and camera transformations together with perspective projection and camera-relative movement.
items: Forward / backward movement using the rotated camera direction

sections.title: 3D Math
paragraphs: I implemented the vector and geometry math used throughout the renderer, lighting, cameras, physics, and procedural systems.

sections.title: Scene & Mesh Architecture
paragraphs: Scene objects owned cameras, mesh collections, lights, ambient-light settings, and render modes.
MeshObject encapsulated reusable geometry with independent position, rotation, color, rendering state, and optional physics state.

sections.title: Model Loading
paragraphs: The pipeline converted external model data into BradEngine's internal mesh representation.

sections.title: Visibility & Depth
paragraphs: The renderer rejected polygons that did not need to be drawn and sorted visible polygons before rendering.

sections.title: Lighting & Render Modes
paragraphs: BradEngine calculated polygon lighting from face normals, directional light vectors, light colors, and ambient light.

sections.title: Procedural Geometry
paragraphs: The renderer could generate geometry in code rather than relying only on imported models.

sections.title: Mesh Morph Animation
paragraphs: BradEngine supported vertex-level mesh morphing between authored model frames.
The animation code advanced through multiple OBJ meshes and linearly interpolated corresponding vertices into the live render mesh.

sections.title: Rigid-Body Physics
paragraphs: Mesh objects could create Cannon.js rigid bodies and synchronize simulated position and rotation back into BradEngine's renderer.

sections.title: Soft-Body / Cloth Physics
paragraphs: Generated plane meshes could be turned into Cannon particle-and-constraint structures.
Simulated particle positions were written back into the mesh vertices so the software renderer displayed the deformation.

sections.title: Three.js Utility Use
paragraphs: Three.js did not render the BradEngine scene.
It was used as a math utility for quaternion-to-Euler conversion when synchronizing Cannon.js physics rotation with BradEngine's own renderer.

sections.title: Terrain & Height Maps
paragraphs: BradEngine's native 3D work also included terrain and height-map-driven geometry as part of the same rendering system.

sections.title: BradEngine Integration
paragraphs: The 3D renderer was integrated with BradEngine's level lifecycle, resource loading, Canvas rendering, input, physics, particles, and reusable project architecture.

historicalNotes: This is the JavaScript BradEngine 3D subsystem; the legacy filename containing 'java-3d-engine' is misleading.
The renderer used JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas.
BradEngine implemented its own transforms, cameras, projection, culling, lighting, polygon sorting, and Canvas drawing.
Three.js did not render the scene in the core pipeline; it was used for quaternion-to-Euler conversion for Cannon.js physics synchronization.
Mesh morphing interpolated corresponding vertices between authored OBJ frames.
Soft-body cloth used Cannon particle bodies and distance constraints with simulated positions written back into mesh vertices.
Voxel-specific systems are intentionally excluded from this card and belong to the dedicated BradEngine Voxel Engine card.
